lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The shuttle ramp hisses shut behind Jack Rook, sealing him into the copper dawn of Dustreach. Fine grit coats the single main street, drifting over boardwalks and the rusted rails that bisect the settlement.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ahead, the colony's last free well sits crowned with a hand-painted sign: "Everyone's Water — No Syndicate Claims." Beyond it, the railway syndicate's prefab headquarters gleams like a fresh wound.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Stranger. You're the only passenger who didn't scurry back aboard.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Sheriff Maya Voss. I'd offer coffee, but the syndicate bought the beans. Brass at the saloon might have something stronger — if his still hasn't blown up again.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Good morning, citizen. Deputy Brass, at your service. The saloon opens in three minutes. I recommend the rotgut; it strips paint and sorrow with equal efficiency.

lines.speaker: Jack Rook
lines.text: Looks like I picked a fine day to arrive.

options: Ask Maya about the well situation
Head to Brass's saloon for information
Walk toward the syndicate headquarters
Check your gear and assess the street

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Jack Rook's boots kick up puffs of rust-colored dust as he walks the length of the main street. The syndicate headquarters looms larger with each step — prefab walls, sensor arrays, a landing pad scorched black by shuttle exhaust.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The saloon sits at the street's far end, a squat structure of riveted steel and salvaged hull plating. A flickering neon sign sputters: "BRASS'S — COLD DRINKS, HOT GOSSIP." The door slides open with a pneumatic sigh.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Ah, the stranger graces us with his presence. Brass polishes a glass with mechanical precision, amber eyes tracking the entrance. The rotgut is... adequately fermented. I also have a vintage synth-whiskey, circa 2280. Tastes like regret and oak chips.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Information, however, is complimentary — provided you survive the evening. The syndicate's water reclamation team arrives on the noon shuttle. They intend to "negotiate" the well's deed. Their negotiator is one Viktor Krane. He does not negotiate.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She leans against the doorframe, hat tipped low, one hand resting on her holster. Brass isn't wrong. Krane's a company man through and through. Bought three moons for the syndicate last year alone. Didn't fire a shot on any of them.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She meets Jack's eyes, expression unreadable. We need that well. The colony dies without it. You've got a fast hand, stranger. Question is — whose side is it on?

options: I'm here for the well. Count me in.
What's in it for me?
Tell me more about Krane first.
I work alone. Give me the details.
result.summary_update: Jack Rook enters Brass's saloon and learns the syndicate's negotiator Viktor Krane arrives at noon to seize the last water well. Sheriff Maya Voss asks Jack to help defend the colony's water supply.

summary: Jack Rook arrives on Dustreach at dawn. Sheriff Maya Voss and android bartender Brass greet him, establishing the conflict: the railway syndicate controls all water wells except one.
Jack Rook enters Brass's saloon and learns the syndicate's negotiator Viktor Krane arrives at noon to seize the last water well. Sheriff Maya Voss asks Jack to help defend the colony's water supply.

player_input.text: Tell me more about Krane first.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She pushes off the doorframe, boot heels clicking on the steel deck. Krane's a ghost story with a expense account. No one's seen his face in five years — just the results.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Colonies sign. Water rights, mineral claims, entire towns — gone before the ink dries. He doesn't threaten. He calculates. Makes you an offer your ledger can't refuse.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: A most apt description, Sheriff. Brass sets down the glass, fingers steepled. My databases indicate Krane was once a colonial administrator. Resigned under... ambiguous circumstances. The syndicate recruited him within the week.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: His signature technique: the "generosity clause." He offers infrastructure, medical supplies, transport credits — everything a struggling colony needs. The deed transfer is buried in appendix twelve, subsection C.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She snorts, a dry sound. And if you read the fine print? You've already signed. The well's output gets metered. Prices rise. Locals can't pay. Within a year, the syndicate owns the aquifer fair and legal.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She fixes Jack with a level gaze. Noon shuttle. Two hours. That's what we've got to find a lever — legal, physical, or otherwise. Brass, you said your archives go back to the founding charter?

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Indeed, Sheriff. The original settlement charter contains a water rights provision. Article Seven, if memory serves. "No external entity shall claim dominion over the colony's primary water source without unanimous consent of the founding families."

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Brass's amber eyes dim slightly, processing. However... the charter requires the signatures of three founding family representatives. Only two remain on Dustreach. The third — Elias Vane — left for the belt mines twelve years ago. Presumed dead.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She straightens, something sharp entering her voice. Not presumed. I've been tracking him. Vane's alive. Working a claim on Asteroid 447-Nemesis. Three days' burn from here.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She looks at Jack, then Brass, then back. If we get Vane's signature before noon... Krane's generosity clause hits a legal wall. The syndicate would need a court order to override — months, minimum.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She lets that hang. But three days there and back? We'd need a fast ship and a pilot crazy enough to run the belt at combat speed. She taps her badge. I know a pilot. Don't know if she's crazy enough.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The saloon's ventilation hum fills the silence. Through the grimy window, the noon shuttle's contrail already streaks the pale sky — a silver needle threading the atmosphere.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: So. Stranger. You want to hear about the pilot, or you got another angle?

options: Ask about the pilot
Suggest a different legal angle
Propose confronting Krane directly
Check if Brass has a ship

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Jack Rook turns to the copper-plated bartender, leaning one hip against the bar's pitted steel surface. The morning light catches dust motes drifting through the ventilation shafts.

lines.speaker: Jack Rook
lines.text: Brass. Which syndicate men have been asking about the last well?

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Brass's amber eyes flicker, pupils contracting as he accesses internal archives. An excellent query, citizen. The syndicate maintains a rotating presence — plausible deniability baked into their operational doctrine.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: However, three individuals have made repeated inquiries at this establishment over the past six weeks. Brass extends a polished finger. First: Mara Vex, logistics coordinator. She has catalogued the well's output, recharge rate, and mineral content on seventeen separate visits. Always orders water. Never alcohol.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Second: Kellen Rook — no relation presumed — a "compliance specialist" whose badge number traces to the syndicate's enforcement division. He has mapped every access point to the aquifer. He asks after the colony's defense capabilities. Casually. Over synth-ale.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: Third... Brass pauses, head tilting with mechanical grace. A woman. No name given. Pale hair, grey coat, cybernetic left eye. She does not drink. She watches. She has attended every town meeting since the syndicate's arrival. The locals call her "The Auditor."

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She crosses her arms, jaw tight. Vex and Rook I knew. The Auditor is new. Or newly visible.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She glances at Jack, one eyebrow raised. That third one worries me. Syndicate doesn't send auditors unless the deal's already structured. They're here to verify the numbers before the ink dries.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She looks back to Brass. Any chatter on when Krane's shuttle touches down? My chrono says forty minutes to noon.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: The noon shuttle's approach vector is locked, Sheriff. Brass returns to polishing his glass, the motion hypnotic. ETA: twelve minutes. Krane typically disembarks first. His retinue follows.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Through the saloon's grimy window, the contrail in the pale sky thickens — a silver thread becoming a rope. Somewhere up there, the noon shuttle burns toward Dustreach.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Twelve minutes. She pushes off the wall, hand settling on her holster. Stranger — pilot's name is Jax Chen. She runs a modified courier ship out of Hangar Three. Fast, reckless, owes me a favor from the Titan incident.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She meets Jack's eyes directly. But she'll need a co-pilot who can handle high-G belt running. And someone to watch her six when Krane's people realize what we're doing. You in? Or you got a different play?

Ask about the Auditor's cybernetic eye
Propose a different strategy to stall Krane
Check your gear before committing

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She nods once, sharp and satisfied. Good. Hangar Three's on the east perimeter — past the ore processors, before the waste reclamation piles. Jax's ship is the Voidskipper, matte black with a scorched starboard nacelle. You can't miss it.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She pulls a folded plastisheet from her duster pocket, unfolds it with a flick of her wrist. Coordinates for 447-Nemesis. Vane's claim beacon frequency. Emergency medevac codes if things go sideways. She holds it out, fingers brushing the worn leather of her holster.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Brass — you're staying. Someone needs to hold the street while we're gone. Keep ears on the syndicate frequency. If Krane moves on the well before we're back...

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: A polite inclination of his copper head. Naturally, Sheriff. I shall maintain the saloon as an intelligence nexus and a sanctuary for any displaced citizens. The rotgut shall flow freely for the righteous. He pauses, amber eyes softening almost imperceptibly. Do return in one piece, both of you. The evening's gossip would be dreadfully dull without you.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Maya tucks the plastisheet into Jack's palm, her calloused fingers lingering a moment longer than necessary. Her green eyes hold his — measuring, weighing.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Twelve minutes to Krane. Three days to the belt and back. She exhales, a sound like wind through dry grass. Let's make time.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The two of them move — Maya striding for the door with purpose, Jack falling into step beside her. Through the saloon's grimy window, the contrail in the pale sky resolves into a descending shape: the noon shuttle, silver and lethal, dropping toward the scorched landing pad beside the syndicate headquarters.

lines.text: The hangar's massive blast doors groan open, swallowing the copper dawn light. Inside, the air smells of ozone, hydraulic fluid, and cold metal. A modified courier ship — matte black, starboard nacelle scorched from some past misadventure — sits anchored to mag-locks, its ramp lowered like a waiting tongue.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She stops at the ramp's edge, one hand raised. Jax! We've got a job. Belt run. Combat speed. Three days there, three back. You in?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A woman drops from the ship's cockpit hatch, landing in a crouch on the deck plates. Late thirties, close-cropped dark hair, flight suit patched at the elbows. She rises, wiping grease from her cheek and only smearing it worse.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Jax Chen. This is Jack Rook. He's riding shotgun. We leave in five minutes — Krane's shuttle touches down in seven.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She sizes Jack up with a pilot's calculating gaze, then grins, sharp and tired. Voidskipper's tanks are full, nav-comp's hot, and I've got stims for the burn. But I need a nav-officer who can plot micro-jumps through the debris field at 447-Nemesis without smearing us across an asteroid.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She jerks her thumb toward the cockpit. You know belt navigation, stranger? Or am I flying blind with a sheriff and a tourist?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She steps closer, voice dropping. Jax — Krane's people are already on the ground. Mara Vex, Kellen Rook, and an Auditor. If they realize we're retrieving Vane...

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Her grin falters, just a fraction. Then we don't let them realize. She climbs back up the ramp, calling over her shoulder. Strap in. We burn in three minutes. Nav station's forward port — if you can keep up.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Maya tosses Jack a comm unit from her belt, then follows the pilot up the ramp. The hangar doors begin their slow grind shut behind them, sealing out the dawn — and the descending silver shape of the noon shuttle, now close enough to read the syndicate logo on its flank.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Voidskipper's interior is a tight squeeze of cable runs, exposed conduit, and the sharp tang of ozone and old coolant. Red standby lighting paints the narrow corridor in emergency hues as the ship's reactor spins up, a low vibration humming through the deck plates.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Jack Rook moves forward past the cramped quarters — two bunks folded against the bulkhead, a hygiene unit that's seen better decades — and drops into the nav station's crash couch. The forward port screens bloom to life: tactical overlay, sensor suite, weapons status.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Twin pulse cannons, dorsal and ventral — charged to ninety percent. A single missile rack, four-shot, loaded with fragmentation warheads. Point-defense laser grid: operational but showing a coolant leak on the starboard emitter. Shield generator: Class Two, rated for micrometeoroid impacts and small-arms fire, not sustained ship-to-ship combat.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Her voice crackles over the ship's intercom, tight with acceleration prep. Nav officer — talk to me. What've we got for teeth?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Maya straps into the aft jump seat, harness clicking home. Her eyes track the external camera feed on the bulkhead screen: the hangar doors still grinding shut, the noon shuttle a silver bullet descending through copper sky.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: We're not looking for a fight, Jax. We're looking for speed. But if Krane's people have a ship watching the belt...

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then we dance. Her grin returns, audible in her voice. Pulse cannons'll shred a patrol boat at close range. Missiles are for discouraging pursuit. The PD laser — keep the starboard side to the enemy if that leak holds.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The deck shudders as mag-locks disengage. Through the forward port, the hangar's blast doors part just enough to spill the ship into the dawning sky. Dustreach falls away below — the main street, the contested well, the syndicate headquarters with its fresh landing pad.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: And there, touching down on that pad as the Voidskipper clears the hangar lip: the noon shuttle. Syndicate logo blazing. Ramp already lowering.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Twelve minutes early. She doesn't sound surprised. Krane doesn't waste time.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Strap in tight, kids. We're lighting the candle.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Three days of hard burn through the debris fields of 447-Nemesis. Three days back. The chrono on the nav console ticks relentlessly — seven minutes since Krane's shuttle touched down. Noon approaches on Dustreach whether they're there or not.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Her fingers dance across the nav-comp, plotting micro-jumps through the thickest debris concentration the belt has to offer. Strap in tight, Sheriff. Nav officer. This ain't a milk run. First jump in thirty seconds.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She checks her comm unit, the plastisheet's coordinates memorized, Vane's beacon frequency locked. Her jaw is set, eyes fixed on the forward screens where asteroids tumble in silent, deadly orbits. Brass — you copy?

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: (over comms, calm and formal) Loud and clear, Sheriff. The noon shuttle has disembarked. Krane is... distinctive. Tall. Grey suit. Left hand prosthetic — military grade. He walks toward the well with Vex and Rook flanking. The Auditor trails behind, recording.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: (over comms) The colony's founding families — the Chen and Okafor representatives — have been located. They are... reluctant. Krane's generosity clause has been presented. Infrastructure promises. Medical supply drops. Transport credits for the young ones.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Her grip tightens on the harness straps. And the deed?

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: (over comms) Forged, Sheriff. Article Seven's signature block has been... altered. A third signature line added, pre-signed with a facsimile of Elias Vane's mark. Krane intends to file it with the planetary registrar before the hour strikes twelve.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She exhales, a sharp sound. Then we bring the real thing. Jax — can you shave time on the return?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Without smearing us? She doesn't look back. Maybe half a day. If the belt doesn't eat us first. Next jump — now.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Voidskipper lurches as the first micro-jump engages, stars stretching into lines, the belt's chaos swallowing them whole. On Dustreach, the clock ticks toward high noon.

lines.text: The Voidskipper screams through the debris field of 447-Nemesis, hull plating pinging with micrometeoroid impacts. Jax Chen's knuckles are white on the flight stick, sweat carving tracks through the grime on her face. Three days compressed into a desperate burn — they've cut corners through the belt that would make a sane pilot weep.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She stares at the chrono, then at the comm unit clutched in her hand. Brass. Talk to me. What's happening at the well?

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: (over comms, formal but strained) Sheriff. The situation has... escalated. Krane has presented the forged deed to the planetary registrar via tightbeam. The Chen and Okafor representatives — under duress, I must add — have affixed their signatures. The third line bears Elias Vane's facsimile.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: (over comms) However. A complication. The Auditor — the cybernetic woman — has just transmitted a priority burst to syndicate headquarters. Encryption broken. She's flagged an anomaly: the Vane signature's biometric hash doesn't match the colonial records.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Her eyes snap to Jack, sharp and sudden. They know it's forged. Or they suspect.

lines.speaker: Brass
lines.text: (over comms) Krane is... negotiating. He's offered the colony a "generosity clause" extension — water at subsidized rates for five years — if the families withdraw their objection to the filing. The registrar's decision is pending. High noon. Twelve minutes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Voidskipper lurches violently as Jax throws it into a hard lateral burn, skimming the gravity well of a tumbling nickel-iron monster. The starboard PD laser coolant alarm screams, a red strobe painting the cockpit in emergency light.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Jax Chen's voice cuts through the chaos, tight and fierce. Nav officer — I need a landing vector for Dustreach that doesn't require a standard approach corridor. We're coming in hot, heavy, and sideways. Can you plot it?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She unstraps, moving aft toward the cargo hatch where a pressure-suited figure waits in cryo-stasis — Elias Vane, revived from his claim's emergency beacon, hollow-eyed and bewildered. He's alive. He's real. And he has a pen.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Jack. Twelve minutes to noon. We hit atmo in eight. She checks her sidearm, then the plastisheet in her other hand — the real Article Seven, the real coordinates, the real beacon frequency. When we land, Krane will have the registrar's ruling. The forged deed. The families' coerced signatures.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She meets Jack's gaze, something fierce and tired burning in her green eyes. What's the play, stranger? We walk in with Vane and the truth? We hit them sideways? You wanted to confront Krane publicly — now's the moment to tell me how.

options: Land hard and march Vane straight to the registrar
Broadcast the forged deed evidence to the whole colony
Have Jax strafe the syndicate HQ as a distraction
Split up: Maya takes Vane legal, Jack confronts Krane direct

The registrar's ruling is pending at high noon — twelve minutes away. Maya asks Jack for the final play.

The third signatory, Elias Vane, is alive on an asteroid claim three days away. Maya knows a pilot but needs a fast ship and crazy pilot to retrieve him before noon.

Maya proposes a plan: retrieve Elias Vane from the asteroid belt using pilot Jax Chen, needing a co-pilot and backup.

player_input.text: I stop hesitating and risk everything right now to settle this once and for all.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Voidskipper's hull groans as Jax Chen hauls the ship into a screaming atmospheric entry, plasma sheathing the forward screens in violent violet. Eight minutes to Dustreach. Eight minutes to noon.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She stands at the cargo hatch, one hand on the manual release, the other clamped on Elias Vane's pressure suit shoulder. The old prospector blinks awake, cryo-fog still clinging to his weather-lined face, eyes darting between the sheriff's badge and Jack's weathered features.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Vane. You know what you're signing. Article Seven. Your mark. Right now. She shoves the plastisheet into his trembling gloved hands, a stylus already activated.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Vane's breath hitches — a ragged sound in the thin ship's air. His gaze finds the starfield through the hatch's small viewport, then the distant curve of Dustreach swelling below. Home. The well. The promise he made thirty years ago.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His hand steadies. The stylus touches 'plas. A signature blooms — shaky, real, biometrically verified. The third line of Article Seven fills with living ink.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She snatches the sheet back, throat working. Got it. Jax — put us down on the main street. In front of the well. Right now.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The pilot's laugh is raw, half-hysterical. Hang onto something, Sheriff. We're not landing. We're arriving.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Voidskipper drops the final thousand meters in a controlled crash, thrusters gouging furrows in the main street's packed dust. The ramp slams down before the ship even stops sliding. Maya is already moving, Vane stumbling behind her, Jack at her flank.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The street goes quiet. Syndicate agents — Vex, Rook, the Auditor — turn as one. Krane stands at the well's control console, prosthetic left hand resting on the forged deed displayed on a holo-projector. The planetary registrar's avatar flickers beside him, awaiting final confirmation.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: High noon. The chrono strikes twelve.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Her voice carries across the sudden silence, amplified by her badge's field. Krane. Registrar. That deed is a lie. She holds up the plastisheet, Vane's fresh signature glowing on the third line. This is the truth. Elias Vane — alive, present, and signing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Auditor's cybernetic eye whirs, aperture dilating. Data streams across her retinal display. The biometric hash matches colonial records. Probability of forgery: less than zero-point-zero-zero-one percent.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Krane's face doesn't change. His prosthetic fingers flex once. A shame. He speaks to the registrar's avatar. The filing stands. The generosity clause —

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Is void. She steps forward, star badge catching the brutal sun. Article Seven requires three living signatures. Not coerced. Not forged. The Chen and Okafor marks were extracted under duress — witnesses?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The crowd that gathered at the edges — miners, families, Brass polishing a glass in the saloon doorway — murmurs. A miner steps forward. Then another. We saw them. Guns at their backs.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The registrar's avatar flickers, processing. New testimony accepted. Duress invalidates signatures. Filing... rejected. The forged deed dissolves. The well's control console flashes green — colony control confirmed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Krane's jaw tightens. The only tell. He looks at Maya. At Jack. At Vane leaning heavy on his cane. This changes nothing. The syndicate owns the railway. The water trains. The supply lines. You have a well. We have the galaxy.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She holsters her sidearm, slow and deliberate. Today we have the well. And the law. She nods to Jack. That's enough for now.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The syndicate agents don't draw. Vex calculates. Rook assesses. The Auditor records. Krane turns, coat sweeping dust, and walks back toward the silver shuttle waiting on the pad. The ramp rises. Engines ignite. They leave.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Brass approaches, bow tie perfectly straight, amber eyes warm. A most satisfactory climax, citizens. Though I suspect the sequel has already been greenlit.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She exhales, a long slow breath that seems to come from somewhere deep. Her green eyes find Jack's. We did it, stranger. The well's ours. The charter holds.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: She extends a calloused hand — not her badge hand. The other one. Partners?

result.summary_update: Jack, Maya, and Jax Chen return to Dustreach with a revived Elias Vane moments before high noon. Vane signs the genuine Article Seven, invalidating Krane's forged deed. The registrar rejects the syndicate's filing after witnesses confirm the founding families signed under duress. Krane departs, vowing the syndicate still controls the supply lines. The colony's last water well is secured.
